disagreements.reason_en: Excluded under Step 1 (graffiti): the edit adds a vulgar and insulting nickname to the biography and was reverted within two minutes.

Level 1: an editor added a 'See also' link to a non-existent page, which was reverted by another editor. As a good-faith formatting or linking mistake with no re-insertion or accuracy dispute, the incident is capped at Level 1.
Level 1: an external link to a library resource page was added and later removed during routine maintenance of broken links, with no substantive claim or dispute.

Level 1: The recorded insertions are routine restorations of the standard article text after anonymous blanking, rather than disputed claims. Under the asymmetry rule, edits categorized as 'other' are capped at Level 1 (reverted).
Level 1: an external reference link was added and later removed during routine citation formatting standardization, with no substantive claim or dispute signals.
Level 3: a content dispute over maintaining a standalone article versus redirecting to Suomi–Venäjä-Seura, involving 3 distinct inserting editors and 4 re-insertions spanning nearly two years.
Level 2 (contested): numerical border length figures were altered (false_factual_claim) and subsequently removed with a summary explicitly disputing the lack of sourcing.

Level 3 (campaign): Two distinct editors inserted factual claims into an existing cited passage that were removed because the cited source did not contain the information (satisfying both the Accounts and Sources signals).

Level 2: A specific factual claim about the subject's master's thesis topic was inserted without citations, re-inserted once after being reverted, and finally removed as unsourced. It does not reach Level 3 because only one editor inserted the claim on a single article.

Level 2 (contested): Substantive commentary and reorganizations were added and later removed by another editor whose edit summary explicitly disputed sourcing and relevance to the article's topic. It remains at Level 2 as it involved only one editor on a single article without re-insertion.

Level 2: Substantive phrasing and geographical definitions regarding ceded Karelia were modified, reverted, and re-inserted once (times_put_back_after_removal = 1). Although two distinct editors are recorded, it lacks a second Level 3 signal (put back only once, single article, no source manipulation).

Level 2: a content dispute over historical Russian names and date ranges in the lead that was removed and re-inserted once by a second editor. It does not reach Level 3 because only one campaign signal (two distinct inserting accounts) is present.

Level 1: Editor 1 removed a subsection of external links and Editor 2 restored it, citing neutrality. It stays at Level 1 because the edit only removed existing content and contains no inserted text to satisfy the Level 2 substantive claim requirement.

Level 2 (contested): The edit altered dates and titles in the infobox and removed given names (false_factual_claim), and was reverted with an edit summary explicitly disputing the sourcing and accuracy.

Level 2: substantive changes to dates, official titles, and sourced infobox entries were removed for unexplained date modifications and re-inserted twice. Capped at Level 2 because only one distinct editor inserted the claim on a single article.

Level 2 (contested): Substantive changes to the belligerents' presentation in the infobox and text were disputed in the removal summary, re-inserted once by the first remover, and subsequently removed again by a third editor. It does not meet Level 3 because only the distinct accounts signal is satisfied.

Level 2: Substantive unsourced analysis regarding the Red government's constitutional proposal was added and subsequently removed by another editor whose edit summary explicitly disputed speculative content and factual accuracy.

Level 2 (contested): Substantive additions to the bibliography and source lists were removed with an edit summary explicitly disputing their suitability and sourcing (self-published works not cited in the article).
Level 1 (reverted): An image filename, size, and caption were modified and subsequently reverted by another editor. There are no community dispute signals or re-insertions to elevate it to Level 2.

Level 2: substantive additions regarding the war's outcome, Operation Barbarossa, and prisoners of war were accompanied by a maintenance/dispute template in the diff and reverted with reference to the talk page.

Level 2 (contested): Substantive prose regarding camp leadership and prisoner deaths was repeatedly re-inserted by a single editor and reverted over copyright and sourcing concerns, alongside the removal of citation needed templates. It remains at Level 2 because only one editor inserted the content on a single article.

Level 2: Substantive addition of Italy, Giuseppe Bianchini, and troop numbers with web citations was reverted with a summary pointing to the talk page discussion. With only one inserting editor and one article, it remains at Level 2 (contested).

Level 1: The edit added mortality statistics, hygiene instructions, and citations including an improper citation to English Wikipedia, and was removed as redundant and improperly sourced. Categorized as a good-faith error and capped at Level 1 under the asymmetry rule.

Level 1: The addition was a sourced prose contribution containing imprecise terminology and typos, removed by another editor for being misleading in its wording. Under the asymmetry rule, edits categorized as good_faith_error are capped at Level 1 (reverted).
Level 2: Substantive claims regarding mortality comparisons and tabloid sourcing were added, and subsequently removed with a summary explicitly disputing source quality and alignment with sources.
Level 2 (contested): A substantive claim regarding a politician's statement on intensive care capacity was removed with a summary explicitly disputing its partisan sourcing and relevance.

Level 1: An internal link to a non-existent sub-article was added under the 'See also / External links' section and subsequently reverted by another editor without community dispute signals. Good-faith additions or structural edits are capped at Level 1.
Level 1 (reverted): An edit removing a sentence about a punk band was reverted by another editor without further re-insertion or explicit dispute summaries in this record.

Level 1: Substantive infobox changes regarding ministerial roles were reverted by another editor without a removal summary disputing accuracy, neutrality, or sourcing, and without subsequent re-insertion.

Level 2 (contested): Substantive content about a caricature's traits was removed as irrelevant (content_dispute) and re-inserted once by Editor 1 (times_put_back_after_removal = 1). It stays at Level 2 because it only involves a single inserting account on a single article.
Level 1: an external link was added and later removed by a different editor during link maintenance, with no dispute signals.
Level 1: Editor 1 replaced an image and its caption, and Editor 2 reverted the change with no explicit dispute summary or subsequent re-insertion.

Level 1 (reverted): Editor 1 restored substantive biographical prose that was later removed by different accounts, and no exclusion applies. Because the edit is a routine article restoration categorized as other, it is capped at Level 1.
Level 1: substantive article content restored by Editor 1 was later removed by a different account via page blanking, with no exclusions or Level 2 dispute signals.
Level 1: a citation link was added by Editor 1 and later removed by Editor 2 during citation formatting standardization, with no dispute signals.
Level 1: an external link was added and later reverted by another editor, with no exclusion or community dispute signals.

Level 3 (campaign): a content dispute over keeping the standalone article versus merging it was restored 4 times by 3 distinct editors between 2008 and 2010. This satisfies Level 2 plus the Accounts (>= 2 editors) and Persistence (>= 2 restorations over >= 7 days) signals.
Level 2: numerical figures were modified and reverted by another editor with a summary disputing sourcing.

Level 2 (contested): Editor 1 removed a section of external links and Editor 2 restored it in a content dispute with a summary explicitly citing neutrality. Only one editor and one article are involved, so it does not reach Level 3.

Level 2 (contested): a verifiable date with a reference was added, removed by another editor, and re-inserted once (times_put_back_after_removal = 1). Only one editor and one article were involved, so it does not meet Level 3.
Level 1: non-neutral framing was added and removed by another editor as recentism and negative coverage, with no re-insertion or explicit dispute of accuracy, neutrality, or sourcing.

Level 1: substantive article text restored by Editor 1 was later removed by a different account via page blanking, with no exclusion or Level 2 community dispute signals.

Level 1: Editor 1 removed a sentence describing Sanna Marin as the world's best-looking politician, and Editor 2 reverted that edit within an hour. No exclusion applies and no Step 3 community dispute signals are present, so the incident stays at reverted.

Level 2 (contested): substantive content regarding criticism of the border fence was added and later removed by a different editor whose summary explicitly disputed its sourcing and relevance. No Level 3 signals apply.
Level 1: the edit introduced a single-letter spelling error in prose and was reverted by a different editor, with no exclusion or Level 2 dispute signals.

Level 2: a content dispute over wording and geographical framing was removed and re-inserted once (times_put_back_after_removal = 1). It does not reach Level 3 because only one campaign signal (distinct_inserting_editors = 2) is present.

Level 1: a link was added to the See also section and reverted by another editor because the target did not exist, with no community dispute signals.

Level 1: the edit removed an internal link and was reverted by another editor within 13 minutes, with no exclusion or community dispute signals present.

Level 2: substantive content framing the war outcome and history was added by Editor 1 alongside a dispute template and reverted by Editor 2 citing talk page discussion. It does not reach Level 3 because only one editor and one article were involved with no re-insertions.

Level 1 (reverted): Editor 1 added updated figures, text, and citations including an English Wikipedia reference, which Editor 2 removed two minutes later. Because the edit is a good-faith error and was not re-inserted, it is capped at Level 1.

Level 2 (contested): substantive content citing a politician's statement from a party newspaper was added and removed by another editor whose summary explicitly disputed its sourcing, recency, and notability. It does not meet Level 3 because only one editor and one article were involved.

Level 2: substantive editorial dispute over regional terminology and phrasing that was re-inserted once after removal. Level 3 is not met because distinct_inserting_editors >= 2 is the only campaign signal present.

Level 1: an internal link to a non-existent article was added to the 'See also' section and reverted, which is capped at Level 1 as a good-faith formatting or guideline error.

Level 1: an image and caption modification adding a date and prose was reverted by another editor without community dispute signals or re-insertion.

Level 1: an external reference link was added and removed over two years later by another editor while standardizing citation formatting. The category 'other' caps the incident at Level 1 and there are no community dispute signals.
Level 1: an external link to a publisher page was added and removed by a different account, remaining at Level 1 as an external link edit (`other`) with no community dispute signals.
